questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Turkmenistan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Climate” part of the Turkmenistan article.

questions.proof: The highest temperature recorded in Ashgabat is 48.0 °C (118.4 °F).

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Turkmenistan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Turkmenistan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Turkmenistan article.

questions.proof: It has borders with Afghanistan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It is slightly smaller than _____ and somewhat larger than the US state of California.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “smaller”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Turkmenistan article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: It is slightly smaller than Spain and somewhat larger than the US state of California.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Köýtendağ is in southeastern Turkmenistan on the borders with _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “borders”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Turkmenistan article, under the heading “Geography”.

questions.proof: Köýtendağ is in southeastern Turkmenistan on the borders with Uzbekistan.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Saparmurat Niyazov became Turkmenistan’s first president in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Turkmenistan article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Saparmurat Niyazov became Turkmenistan’s first president in 1991.
